es: Distinguir el significado literal del implícito en réplicas cortas de la vida diaria y elegir la interpretación coherente con el contexto.

teaching.en: It's a bit cold in here can be a hint that you should close the window.
teaching.es: «Hace un poco de frío aquí» puede ser una indirecta para que cierres la ventana.
teaching.explanationEs: La frase habla de la temperatura (literal), pero el hablante pide algo (implícito).
segments: It's a bit cold in here can be

teaching.en: Some of us have been working all morning can imply that you have not helped.
teaching.es: «Algunos llevamos toda la mañana trabajando» puede dar a entender que tú no has ayudado.
teaching.explanationEs: Imply: la frase no acusa, pero el oyente deduce la crítica.
segments: Some of us have been working all morning
can imply that you have not helped.
teaching.audioText: Some of us have been working all morning can imply that you have not helped.

teaching.en: The literal meaning of Great timing is positive, but her tone shows that she is annoyed.

teaching.explanationEs: Literal es lo que dicen las palabras; el tono puede cambiar el mensaje.
segments: The literal meaning of Great timing is positive,

teaching.en: His reply was I'll think about it, and everyone understood that he meant no.
teaching.es: Su respuesta fue «lo pensaré» y todos entendieron que quería decir que no.
teaching.explanationEs: Una réplica educada puede esconder un rechazo; el contexto lo revela.
segments: His reply was I'll think about it,
and everyone understood that he meant no.
teaching.audioText: His reply was I'll think about it, and everyone understood that he meant no.

teaching.en: When people complain politely, the hidden message is often in the context, not in the words.
teaching.es: Cuando la gente se queja con educación, el mensaje oculto suele estar en el contexto, no en las palabras.
teaching.explanationEs: Hidden message: lo que no se dice; búscalo en quién habla y en qué situación.
segments: When people complain politely, the hidden message is

prompt.es: Elige qué quiere decir de verdad Ana con su frase.

choices.text: I am afraid of the dark.
I need a new watch.
I want to go home.

feedback.es: Con el abrigo puesto y mirando el reloj, su frase sobre la hora es una indirecta: quiere irse.

hint.es: Fíjate en lo que hace Ana mientras habla.

origin.text: Ana lleva el abrigo puesto, mira el reloj y dice: «It's getting late.»

prompt.es: Completa: «El significado literal de sus palabras es sí, pero quería decir no.»

answer.text: literal

feedback.es: Literal es lo que dicen las palabras; lo que el hablante quiere decir de verdad es el significado implícito.

hint.es: Es lo contrario de implícito: lo que dicen las palabras.

origin.text: The ___ meaning of his words is yes, but he meant no.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Sus palabras dan a entender que llegamos tarde.»

answer.text: Her words imply that we are late

feedback.es: Imply va seguido de that + oración: el sujeto (her words) es quien da a entender.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué le sugiere ella a él sin decirlo.

choices.text: She hints that he should leave now.
She asks about the train timetable.
She is surprised he has a ticket.

feedback.es: No pide horarios: al recordar la hora de su tren y decir que ya casi es, insinúa que debe salir ya.

origin.audio: Isn't your train at six? It's ten to six already.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada réplica con lo que quiere decir de verdad.

feedback.es: Cada réplica dice algo literal distinto de su mensaje: una queja por el ruido, un rechazo cortés y una crítica sobre el café.

prompt.es: Elige la interpretación más coherente con el contexto.

choices.text: She will lend you the bike tomorrow.
She is politely saying no.
She is excited about the idea.

feedback.es: Cambiar de tema tras la réplica es la pista: rechaza con cortesía sin decir no.

origin.text: Tu hermana responde «I'll think about it» cuando le pides la bici, cambia de tema y no vuelve a mencionarlo.

prompt.es: Escucha al anfitrión y elige qué pide a sus invitados sin decirlo.

choices.text: He wants to start work now.
He wants to know the time.
He wants his guests to leave.

feedback.es: Quien menciona la hora y su madrugón no informa: pide que los invitados se vayan.

origin.audio: It's nearly midnight, and I have an early start tomorrow.

prompt.es: Elige lo que Carlos da a entender con su frase.

choices.text: He hints that they should ask for the bill.
He is reading the sign on the door.
He wants to work in the kitchen.

feedback.es: Es casi la hora de cierre y falta la cuenta: la información literal sirve de indirecta para pedirla ya.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Su respuesta daba a entender que no vendría.»

answer.text: His reply implied that he would not come

feedback.es: Implied + that + oración muestra que el mensaje no se dice: lo sugiere su respuesta.

prompt.es: Elige cómo cuenta Mia que su vecino se quejó del ruido.

choices.text: My neighbour complained me about the noise.
My neighbour complained to me about the noise.
My neighbour complained for me the noise.

feedback.es: Complain se construye con to (a quién) y about (de qué): complained to me about the noise.

prompt.es: Elige qué quiere decir tu compañera de verdad.

choices.text: She is proud of her own desk.
She asks you to tidy her desk.
She hints that your desk is a mess.

feedback.es: Elogiar el orden ajeno mientras miras un escritorio desordenado es una crítica indirecta.

origin.text: Una compañera mira tu escritorio desordenado y dice: «Some people keep their desks very tidy.»

answer.text: The hidden message is in the context

feedback.es: Hidden describe el mensaje que no se dice; el contexto es donde se encuentra.

es: Interpretar coletillas de misma polaridad como reto, burla o reproche y distinguirlas de las coletillas que piden confirmar un dato.

teaching.en: You didn't promise to pay, did you?
teaching.es: No prometiste pagar, ¿verdad?
teaching.explanationEs: Frase negativa + coletilla afirmativa (polaridad opuesta): pregunta de verdad y pide confirmar un dato.
segments: You didn't promise to
pay, did you?
teaching.audioText: You didn't promise to pay, did you?

teaching.en: Oh, you're the expert now, are you?
teaching.es: Vaya, ¿ahora eres tú el experto, eh?
teaching.explanationEs: Frase afirmativa + coletilla afirmativa (misma polaridad): no pide datos, se burla.
segments: Oh, you're the expert
now, are you?
teaching.audioText: Oh, you're the expert now, are you?

teaching.en: You can fix it by yourself, can you?

segments: You can fix it
by yourself, can you?
teaching.audioText: You can fix it by yourself, can you?

teaching.en: Too lazy to cook, are you?

teaching.en: Turn the music down, will you? The baby is asleep.

segments: Turn the music down, will
you? The baby is asleep.
teaching.audioText: Turn the music down, will you? The baby is asleep.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que pide confirmar un dato (polaridad opuesta).

choices.text: You didn't promise to help, did you?
You promise to help, do you?
You didn't promise to help, didn't you?

feedback.es: La coletilla de verdad lleva polaridad opuesta a la frase: negativa + did you?, que pide confirmar.

hint.es: Si la frase es negativa, la coletilla de verdad es afirmativa.

prompt.es: Completa: «Vaya, ¿ahora eres tú el jefe, eh?»

answer.text: are

feedback.es: Misma polaridad: la coletilla repite el verbo en afirmativo (are you?) y suena a burla.

hint.es: Repite el verbo be de la frase, sin negar.

origin.text: Oh, you're the boss now, ___ you?

answer.text: You can fix that bike can you

hint.es: La coletilla repite can sin not.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opina ella de lo que dice él.

choices.text: She asks what homework there is.
She doubts that he has really finished.
She is proud and wants to thank him.

feedback.es: Frase y coletilla afirmativas: no pide información, duda de que lo haya terminado.

pairs: Too tired to help, are you?

feedback.es: Las dos primeras repiten la polaridad (reto y reproche); la tercera la cambia y pregunta de verdad.

pairs: Too tired to help, are you?

prompt.es: Elige la coletilla que muestra duda en lugar de preguntar de verdad.

choices.text: You didn't finish it in ten minutes, did you?
You finished it in ten minutes, didn't you?

feedback.es: Para dudar se mantiene la polaridad: afirmativa + did you?; las otras cambian la polaridad y piden confirmar.

choices.text: He checks that the tickets are safe.
He challenges a lazy friend.

feedback.es: Polaridad opuesta: pregunta de verdad para confirmar que las entradas no se olvidaron.

origin.text: So you ate the whole pizza alone, ___ you?

prompt.es: Ordena: «Olvidaste las llaves otra vez, ¿eh?»

answer.text: You forgot your keys again did you

feedback.es: La coletilla did you? repite el pasado en afirmativo y reprocha el olvido.

prompt.es: Elige la intención de «Too tired to walk, are you?».

choices.text: To ask for real information.
To tease or reproach someone.
To confirm a fact he already knows.

feedback.es: Sin cambio de polaridad, la coletilla no busca datos: se burla o reprocha.

prompt.es: Elige la coletilla correcta para «No puedes arreglarlo, ¿verdad?».

choices.text: You can't fix it, isn't it?
You can't fix it, can't you?
You can't fix it, can you?

prompt.es: Completa: «Cállate, ¿quieres? Estoy al teléfono.»

choices.text: She doubts that he will really do it.

prompt.es: Escribe qué quiere cada pariente y cómo respondes.

answer.text: My mother asks if that is all I'm having, so she wants me to eat more. My grandmother says nobody asks for seconds, so she hopes that I will ask. My uncle says some relatives only call when they need something, so he is hinting that I do not call enough. Mum, I couldn't eat another bite, but the dessert looks lovely, doesn't it? Grandma, everything is delicious, so I'll have some later, if that's all right. Uncle, I'm sorry I've been busy, but I'll call more often, won't I?
accepted: My mother asks if that is all I'm having, so she wants me to eat more. My grandmother says nobody asks for seconds, so she hopes that I will ask. Grandma, everything is delicious, so I'll have some later, if that's all right. Uncle, I'm sorry I've been busy, but I'll call more often, won't I?
